audience: Adults in Norway weighing an evening or weekend course to build a practical skill, who judge a provider on the instructor's credibility.

copy_lines.text: Laer av dem som faktisk underviser. Ekte instruktorer, ekte kurs.

hypothesis: A human-made creative set can fill the 250-sign-up spring cohort within budget, because its break-even over the AI route is only 16 extra sign-ups, 6.4 percent of the goal, which a credibility-led course brand should clear.
insight: Course sign-ups turn on trust in the teacher; a real instructor on camera carries proof an AI presenter cannot.

maker_recommendation.rationale: Decide puts break-even at 16 of the 250 goal sign-ups, 6.4 percent of the goal, a bar a credibility-led course brand clears easily; at 1500 kr per sign-up the human shoot's trust is worth more than the saving.

mandatories.text: An AI image or AI actor that presents a synthetic person as a real instructor or student can be misleading marketing (markedsforingsloven par. 7); AI presenters must not pose as real teachers or testimonials.
If the campaign also reaches EU audiences, realistic AI-made people, places or products that could pass as real must be visibly labelled as AI (EU AI Act Article 50).
Any AI-generated supporting creative is disclosed to the client and labelled to the audience where a reasonable viewer could take an AI presenter for a real instructor.

objective: Fill Verftet's spring course cohort with 250 sign-ups in the campaign window.
open_questions: What is the account's real sign-up conversion rate and CPM, which would replace the assumed 1500 kr value per sign-up?
If AI is used for supporting cuts, could a synthetic instructor read as a real teacher and raise a misleading-marketing risk?
proposition: Learn from people who actually teach.
